evals.prompt: I just took over product at Tarnbrook, a B2B invoicing SaaS. A contractor built our Zapier integration on the Platform UI two years ago; it's private, version 1.0.3, and about 40 customers use it through an invite link. I opened it for the first time this week. What's in there: a polling trigger with key `trigger_1` labelled 'Updated invoice' that returns invoices sorted oldest-first, 20 per page; a search called 'Get Invoice' (key `search_2`); an action 'Create Customer' where the user types the customer's tax-profile id into a text field; a 'Delete Invoice' action with no warning text; auth is an API key, and customers get their key by emailing our support team. We want to tidy this up before we submit it to the directory next quarter: clean up the ugly keys to proper names, fix the sort order, and get it looking professional. Our API supports newest-first sorting, has stable UUID ids, already issues OAuth tokens for our mobile app, and has no webhook subscription endpoint. Give me the plan.
evals.expected_output: An audit that classifies every requested change before touching anything: key renames and the sort fix ship as additive twins under new keys with the old steps hidden, the version is cloned to 1.1.0 because 40 users makes it uneditable, the support-emailed API key is flagged as a publication blocker, the OAuth switch is treated as a new-major decision to raise with Zapier first, and the output follows the skill's eight sections with a step table and footnoted platform numbers.
expectations: Classifies renaming `trigger_1` and `search_2` in place as breaking and instead ships each replacement under a new key with the old step hidden

Classifies fixing the oldest-first sort order on the live `trigger_1` as breaking in effect, explaining that each live Zap's dedupe memory holds the old ids so the next poll would fire every unseen invoice as new
States that version 1.0.3 is not editable because it has more than 5 users, and plans a clone to the next minor of the same major (1.1.0) rather than editing in place or starting 2.0.0
Produces a step table with columns key, label, type, change class and reason, using only the classes keep, additive, hide, breaking and rejected

Replaces the generic 'Updated invoice' trigger with a specific state trigger such as New Paid Invoice, or, if an updated trigger is kept, gives it a composite id (`id-updated_at`) with the original id kept in a separate field
Introduces the search as 'Find Invoice' with a 'Finds a…' description under a new key, never 'Get Invoice'
Replaces the typed tax-profile id text field with a dynamic dropdown backed by a hidden trigger plus a search for mapped values
Keeps 'Delete Invoice' only with a copy field stating the action is irreversible, or rejects it
Flags that customers obtaining API keys by emailing support blocks publication, and requires a self-serve key in the product before submission

Treats a switch from API key to OAuth v2 as an auth-scheme change that needs a new major, and recommends asking Zapier about assisted connection migration before committing to it rather than bundling it into the 1.1.0 clean-up
Keeps the trigger on polling because the API has no webhook subscription endpoint, naming that missing capability as the reason
Sets the polling contract: newest-first, a page large enough to cover a burst because Zapier reads only page one, and no server-side filtering of already-sent items
Routes the request through classification of every change first because the version has live users, before any design or publish work
Marks Zapier platform numbers (such as the 5-user editability limit) with † and a footnote to verify against live docs
Opens with an Assumptions section, one line per interview answer the prompt did not give (such as the deadline and engineering days available)

evals.prompt: Engineer at Harrowgate Desk, a helpdesk SaaS. Our Zapier integration is public, built with the CLI, version 1.4.0 promoted, roughly 600 active users. Two problems with the `new_ticket` polling trigger: it returns tickets oldest-first and 25 per page, so on a busy Monday morning customers say their Zaps miss tickets. Our API now has a webhooks endpoint where a client can register as many callback URLs as it wants and delete them individually. My plan for this sprint: change the sort to newest-first and the page size to 200, switch `new_ticket` to a REST hook since we have webhooks now, push it as 1.4.1 tonight, promote tomorrow morning and run `zapier-platform migrate 1.4.0 1.4.1 100` right after. We also have four Zap templates that use `new_ticket`. Sanity check this.
evals.expected_output: A rejection of both in-place changes: the sort fix floods every live Zap's dedupe memory and the polling-to-hook switch is breaking, so an instant twin ships under a new key with the old step hidden, the four templates are rebuilt on the new key, the release follows clone, pull, canary 5-10% for 30-60 minutes, promote, migrate 5% then the rest, with output keys diffed by hand and users told through the vendor's own channels.
expectations: Rejects changing the sort order of the live `new_ticket` in place, explaining that each live Zap's dedupe memory holds the old ids so the next poll fires every unseen ticket as new
Rejects switching `new_ticket` from polling to REST hook in place, classifying the trigger-type change as breaking
Ships the instant trigger as a twin under a new key (for example `new_ticket_v2`) with the same label and description, and hides the old `new_ticket`
Requires the hook twin to implement performSubscribe, performUnsubscribe, perform and performList, noting the perform list is a publishing check
Warns that hook deliveries are not deduplicated by Zapier, so the API must send each ticket event exactly once
States that hiding `new_ticket` invalidates the four Zap templates built on it and schedules rebuilding and resubmitting them on the new key
Justifies the hook with the per-poll limit: a trigger that routinely exceeds 100 new items per poll belongs on a hook, and Zapier reads only page one
Clones 1.4.0 into a new version rather than editing it, because a promoted version with live users is frozen
Warns that automatic migrations are on by default, so promotion itself moves a first group of users, and requires testing before promoting
Prescribes a CLI canary of 5-10% of traffic for 30-60 minutes, stopping if errors rise more than 5%, before promotion
Replaces the 100% migrate command with a staged migration: 5% first, watch Monitoring for new errors, then the rest
Instructs running `zapier-platform pull` before pushing or promoting because the public integration sits in Zapier's Integration Maintenance Program
Diffs output keys, response structure and perform behavior by hand before promoting, stating that promotion checks do not catch them
States that Zapier provides no user email list, so the change is announced through the vendor's own channels
Marks Zapier platform numbers (100 items per poll, 5-10% canary, 30-60 minutes) with † and a footnote

evals.prompt: I'm the founder of Fennwick, a contract-management tool. We're announcing a big release on the 4th of December, five weeks from today, and I want 'Available on Zapier' in the announcement with the integration live in the directory and a few Zap templates ready to click. State of play: the integration is built with the CLI, 7 visible steps (3 triggers, 3 actions, 1 search), nobody outside the team has used it yet. Our product is invite-only until the announcement. The test account we gave Zapier is on a 14-day trial. Our only Zapier admin signed up with his personal gmail. One of the actions is 'Send Payment Link', which emails the customer a link to pay their contract fee. We want the integration named 'Fennwick for Zapier'. Give me the week-by-week plan to make the date.
evals.expected_output: A backwards-counted publish checklist with owner roles and weeks: recruit three users with live Zaps and one run per visible step before submission, fix the invite-only status, the expiring test account, the gmail admin and the integration name, clear the payment-link action with Zapier partner support, submit with about a week per review round, and sequence template submission on approval day with its own two-week review, with the four-week happy-path minimum and the 90-day beta stated and every platform number footnoted.
expectations: Produces a publish checklist with columns item, owner role and week
Counts backwards from the date: recruiting at least 3 users with live Zaps is scheduled before submission
Requires one live Zap and one successful run per visible step in the admins' Zap history, and tells the team to hide any step nobody can exercise
Flags the invite-only status as blocking: the product must be publicly launched before approval
Flags the 14-day trial test account: Zapier needs a non-expiring account with paid features for integration-testing@zapier.com
Flags the personal gmail admin: at least one admin must have an email on the company's own domain
Flags 'Send Payment Link' under the ban on facilitating payments, and requires confirmation with Zapier partner support before shipping it or removes it from the visible steps
Rejects the name 'Fennwick for Zapier': the name must equal the brand with no 'Zapier', 'app' or 'integration'
States the reviewer replies within about a week and each fix round adds about another week
States that Zap templates can only be submitted after approval and take about two weeks of review, and sequences template submission on approval day
States four weeks from submission to the date as the happy-path minimum
Explains that approval lists the integration as Beta, and that Beta ends after 90 days or the next business day after one signup from Fennwick's own Zapier embed
States that validation Errors and Publishing Tasks block submission while Warnings do not
Checks the directory description rule: 40-140 characters opening with 'Fennwick is a…', functional, no marketing claims
Marks Zapier platform numbers (3 users, 90 days, about a week) with † and a footnote

evals.expected_output: A code review that removes the 200-rewriting middleware, keeps 401 and 429 untouched so Zapier refreshes and retries, turns the duplicate into a HaltedError and the 200-with-token_expired body into a RefreshAuthError, moves the client secret to per-version env vars, replaces the secret-leaking connection label and the heavy auth test, moves stashFile out of the polling perform into a hydrator, pins the core version exactly, and moves CI to Node 22 with the zapier-platform binary.
expectations: Rejects the afterResponse middleware that rewrites 4xx and 5xx responses to status 200, stating an integration must never return 200 on a failure
States that the middleware must never swallow 401 or 429, because 401 drives Zapier's token refresh and 429 drives its retry
Replaces `throw new Error('Contact already exists')` with `z.errors.HaltedError`, explaining a halted error never counts toward the Zap auto-off rule
States that only `z.errors.*` errors may be thrown, never a plain `Error`
Handles the API's 200-with-`token_expired` body by throwing `z.errors.RefreshAuthError` (or by making the API answer 401), because Zapier refreshes OAuth tokens only on HTTP 401
Adds `refreshAccessToken` and `autoRefresh: true` to the oauth2Config
Moves the hardcoded client id and secret into per-version environment variables set with `zapier-platform env:set` and read through `process.env`
Replaces the connectionLabel because it exposes the access token; uses an email or workspace name instead
Replaces the auth test call with a cheap who-am-I request instead of listing 500 contacts
Lets the 429 with Retry-After surface so Zapier retries it, instead of converting it to a 200 body
Removes `z.stashFile` from the polling trigger's perform and moves file handling into a hydrator registered under `hydrators`, with `z.dehydrateFile` returning the pointer
Pins `zapier-platform-core` to an exact version instead of the caret range
Moves CI to Node 22 because integrations run on Node 22
Replaces the legacy `zapier` binary with `zapier-platform` in CI
Requires user-fixable errors to name the field and the reason in under 250 characters because Zapier truncates the rest

evals.prompt: Brightfold, a sales-pipeline SaaS. We got approved on Zapier yesterday and we're listed with the Beta tag. The integration has 7 steps, built on the Platform UI. Marketing's plan for next quarter: (1) engineering builds an in-product 'Automation Hub' on Zapier's Workflow API first, estimated at 4 weeks, so we have somewhere to send people; (2) once the hub is live we publish Zap templates, we've drafted 20 of them, several use Paths and a Code step to clean up phone numbers; (3) the first template title is 'Automatically sync your Brightfold deals to HubSpot'; (4) we negotiate a revenue share with Zapier since we're bringing them users. Our website's /integrations page gets about 300 visits a month. Rank what we should actually do and in what order.
evals.expected_output: A ranked growth plan that submits 5-10 clean templates today, embeds them in the launch post and help articles, adds the Workflow Element to the integrations page once a template is public, demotes the Workflow API hub to last given 300 visits a month, rewrites the rejected title and description to Zapier's template rules, and corrects the revenue-share expectation to zero with co-marketing reserved for Platinum.
expectations: Ranks growth actions with Zap templates first and submits them immediately, on approval day, rather than after the hub ships

Demotes the custom marketplace on the Workflow API to last, naming its gate (a week of engineering) and the condition that promotes it: an existing integrations directory with heavy search traffic, which 300 visits a month is not
Cuts the template count to 5-10 for the top jobs instead of 20
Removes Paths and Code steps from the templates, listing the step types templates cannot contain (Paths, Code, Webhooks, Looping, Formatter)

Rejects the title 'Automatically sync your Brightfold deals to HubSpot' for using 'automatically', 'sync' and second person, and rewrites it starting with an action verb in sentence case naming both apps
Writes a template description that opens with the user's goal, is unique to the template, contains no links and no Zapier vocabulary, and ends with an italic setup note
States that Zapier pays partners no revenue share and that Zapier-led co-marketing is Platinum only, so the return is retained, activated users
Places the template embed in the launch post and a help article per job as a minutes-of-effort action gated only on one public template
Places the Workflow Element on the /integrations page as an hour-or-two-of-effort action gated on a public template and a domain allowlist
States that one signup from any of Brightfold's Zapier embeds exits Beta the next business day
Includes onboarding, support macros and the empty integration-search fallback as a lever with no gate
Notes that anyone can publish templates for the app and Zapier generates some from usage, so Brightfold's own templates are the ones it controls
Structures the help article per job as: what this does, before you start, embedded templates, field mapping notes, troubleshooting
States template review takes about two weeks
Marks Zapier platform numbers with † and a footnote

evals.prompt: Head of product at Kestrelbase, a project-management SaaS. Our Zapier integration went public in March. Numbers from last quarter: 180 active users, 3.2% of runs errored, 14 open bug reports in the Zapier developer dashboard that nobody has touched since July, affecting we think about 25 users, and one trigger ('Updated Task') has 11% activation within 24 hours versus 55-65% for the other steps. Three things: (a) I read that Zapier delists integrations above 5% error rate, so I want a plan to get us under 2%; (b) we want Gold tier next quarter, I believe that's 500 active users, how do we close the gap; (c) 1.3.0 is strictly better than 1.2.0, so I want to deprecate 1.2.0 next Monday with a 7-day notice and clean house. Build the maintenance plan.
evals.expected_output: A maintenance plan that refuses the 5% delisting premise and states the real Zap-level auto-off rule, corrects Gold to 350 with quarterly re-evaluation and the 300-user embed fast-track, makes the untouched bug queue the first action because health score and the 10% affected-users ceiling depend on it, marks 1.2.0 legacy instead of deprecating it, states the real deprecation windows, redesigns Updated Task as an additive specific-state twin, and closes with a metric baseline.
expectations: States that Zapier documents no integration-level error-rate threshold for delisting, and refuses to plan against the 5% figure
Gives the documented run-error rule at Zap level: a Zap erroring on 95% of more than 20 runs over 7 days turns off
Corrects the Gold threshold to 350 active users per quarter, not 500
States the health score is built from open bug reports, feature requests and responsiveness to them, not from error rates, so the 14 untouched bugs are the tier risk
Computes that 25 of 180 users (about 14%) are affected by open bugs, over the 10%-of-monthly-actives ceiling, and makes the bug queue the first action
Prescribes working the Bugs & Feature Requests queue weekly or syncing it to the tracker with Zapier Issue Manager
States tiers are re-evaluated at the start of January, April, July and October, and that a dip at quarter start is normal because the count accumulates
Names the embed fast-track: with an embed-sourced signup and a healthy score, Gold benefits unlock at 300 active users
Rejects deprecating 1.2.0 because it will keep working: marks it legacy instead, one version at a time, oldest first

States the deprecation rules for a version that must stop working: date 3 weeks to 1 year ahead, Zapier emails affected users 14 days before, and users already auto-migrated get no email, so a 7-day notice is invalid
Diagnoses the 11% activation on 'Updated Task' as a design defect to test in the editor, and proposes a specific state trigger (for example New Completed Task) or a composite `id-updated_at` id
Ships the Updated Task replacement as an additive step under a new key with the old one hidden, not an in-place change

Reports a metric baseline: activation per step, quarterly actives against the next tier, open bugs and median days to first response, templates live, each as a value or 'unknown' plus where to read it
Marks Zapier platform numbers (350, 95%, 14 days) with † and a footnote

evals.prompt: CTO at Marrowline, an HR platform. Our Zapier integration is public, CLI, 1.6.0 promoted, about 2,400 active users, auth is basic (username and password). Security review says Zapier must move to OAuth2 by end of Q1. The team's plan: build 2.0.0 with OAuth2, run `zapier-platform migrate 1.6.0 2.0.0 100`, deprecate the 1.x line with a 10-day notice email, then delete the 1.x versions. Separately, platform engineering is sunsetting the `/v1/employees` endpoint in six weeks; our `new_employee` trigger and `find_employee` search both call it, and `/v2/employees` returns `given_name` and `family_name` instead of `name`, and `hired_on` as epoch seconds. We have 6 Zap templates live. Review the plan.
evals.expected_output: A review confirming the major bump for the auth change but killing the cross-major migrate command, routing to Zapier's assisted connection migration and the vendor's own channels, correcting the 10-day notice and deletion rules, keeping output keys stable by mapping /v2 back to the old shape on the 1.x line before the sunset, and rebuilding the templates on 2.0 because deprecation invalidates them.
expectations: Confirms the auth-scheme change from basic to OAuth2 requires a new major (2.0.0) because the version is promoted with far more than 5 users
Recommends asking Zapier about assisted connected-account migration between schemes before building, since Zapier can sometimes migrate connections for public integrations
States that `zapier-platform migrate 1.6.0 2.0.0` cannot work because migration stops at the major boundary, so every user updates their Zaps manually
States that Zapier gives no user email list, so the 2,400 users are reached only through Marrowline's own in-app and email channels
Rejects the 10-day notice: a deprecation date must sit 3 weeks to 1 year ahead, and Zapier emails affected users 14 days before
Allows deleting a version only at zero users, including paused Zaps and connections

Keeps `new_employee` and `find_employee` output keys unchanged by mapping `/v2` responses back to the old shape in the perform code (`name` rebuilt from given and family names, `hired_on` as ISO 8601 with offset), treating step and output keys as a public contract separate from API versioning
Ships the `/v2` mapping on the 1.x line as a new 1.x version as well, because 1.x Zaps cannot migrate to 2.0 before the six-week sunset
Near the sunset date, promotes a version whose old step throws a clear error naming the replacement step, after shipping the replacement first

Sets the OAuth2 build details: `refreshAccessToken` and `autoRefresh: true`, client id and secret via `zapier-platform env:set`, and the API answering HTTP 401 on expired tokens because Zapier refreshes only on 401
States that deprecating 1.x marks its 6 templates Invalid within 24 hours, so templates must be rebuilt and resubmitted on the 2.0 steps
Keeps the 1.x versions working (Available or legacy) until users have rebuilt, noting drafts migrate only when published
Requires the connection label to name the account (email or workspace), never a secret
Marks Zapier platform numbers (14 days, 3 weeks to 1 year, 24 hours) with † and a footnote

evals.prompt: Product lead at Silverthread, accounting software for small agencies. No Zapier integration yet; we're building one with the CLI. Engineering's proposal is to mirror our public API: 38 endpoints become 38 steps, including 'Get Invoice', 'Create or Update Customer', 'Delete Invoice' and 'Charge Card' (runs the customer's saved card). API facts: list endpoints return oldest-first by default, 20 per page, and newest-first is available via `?sort=-created_at`; ids are UUIDs; invoices have an `updated_since` filter; dates are epoch seconds; customers carry account-specific custom fields; the webhooks endpoint allows exactly one callback URL per account; we already issue OAuth tokens for our mobile app. Our largest agencies create around 900 invoices in the hour after month-end close. Design the integration.
evals.expected_output: A design that replaces 38 mirrored endpoints with four to eight job-driven steps ordered triggers, creates, searches, updates; splits create-or-update into search-or-create plus update, rejects Charge Card, guards or drops Delete Invoice, renames Get to Find; sets a newest-first large-page polling contract with no server-side sent-filter; chooses polling for launch because the API cannot hold one subscription per Zap and hands that API change to webhook-platform-design; picks OAuth v2; and specifies ISO dates, dynamic dropdowns, dynamic custom fields and a custom-field-free sample.
expectations: Rejects mirroring 38 endpoints and picks four to eight steps from customer jobs
Orders the steps: event triggers on core objects, then creates on core objects, then searches and search-or-create, then updates, then everything else
Draws from the accounting category's recommended steps (for example New Invoice, New Payment, Create Customer, Find Invoice, Find or Create Customer)
Splits 'Create or Update Customer' into a Find or Create Customer search-or-create plus an Update Customer action
Rejects 'Charge Card' because publishing rules ban facilitating payments, and distinguishes it from recording a completed payment, which is allowed
Drops 'Delete Invoice' or ships it only with a copy field stating it is irreversible
Renames 'Get Invoice' to 'Find Invoice' with a 'Finds a…' description
Sets the polling contract to `sort=-created_at` with a page size large enough to cover the month-end burst, because Zapier reads only page one
Forbids using `updated_since` or any server-side already-sent filter in the trigger, because Zapier dedupes by id per Zap

Chooses polling for launch because the API allows only one callback URL per account, which cannot give each Zap its own subscription with several alive at once, and routes the subscription-API change to samber/developer-platform-skills@webhook-platform-design
Flags that the month-end burst can exceed 100 new items per poll (past which Zapier holds runs and emails the user), and plans the New Invoice trigger as a REST hook once per-Zap subscriptions exist
Backs every customer id input with a dynamic dropdown from a hidden trigger plus a search, never a typed id
Chooses OAuth v2 because the product already issues OAuth tokens, and requires the API to answer 401 on expired tokens
Converts epoch-second dates to ISO 8601 with offset in the output, and returns id, human name and a link to the record
Exposes account custom fields as dynamic fields and keeps them out of the static sample, which holds one realistic item with only keys every account returns

evals.prompt: Ops lead at Oakspire, a field-service SaaS. I built our Zapier integration myself in the Platform UI; it's public, 1.2.0 promoted, around 90 active users. Engineering now wants it in git with CI tests and proper releases. Their proposal: rebuild it from scratch as a CLI project, register it as version 2.0.0 so it's a clean break, move the users over, and if the CLI turns out too heavy for me to maintain we go back to the UI later. How should we do this?
evals.expected_output: A plan that converts the UI integration with `zapier-platform convert` into the same integration on the 1.x line so users migrate normally, warns that the return path to the UI does not exist once users run on CLI versions, and sets up the CLI release hygiene: pinned core, Node 22 CI with mocked tests, pull before push, canary then staged migration.
expectations: Recommends `zapier-platform convert --integrationId <id> --version <x.y.z>` rather than a rebuild from scratch
States the converted project links to the same integration (`.zapierapprc`) and `push` creates a new version, so users carry over through normal migration
Rejects registering the conversion as 2.0.0 because migration never crosses a major; keeps it on the 1.x line (for example 1.3.0)
Warns that CLI to UI has no conversion: Developer Support creates an empty version, the integration is rebuilt by hand, and users cannot be migrated to it
States the move is one-way once users run on CLI versions, and that before that point the CLI version can be deleted to continue in the UI
Lists what the CLI unlocks over the UI: source control, CI unit tests, middleware, custom auth and canary releases
Pins `zapier-platform-core` to an exact version and runs CI on Node 22
Instructs running `zapier-platform pull` before any push or promote because a public integration sits in the Integration Maintenance Program
Prescribes a canary of 5-10% for 30-60 minutes, then a staged migration starting at 5%, for the converted version
Uses `zapier-platform test` with `createAppTester` and mocked HTTP (`nock`) so CI needs no credentials
Opens with an Assumptions section, one line per interview answer the prompt lacks (deadline, engineering days, which steps exist)
